says: In next/, the law `L1: every prefix keeps the pinned tree after checkout edits, branch switches and origin moves` fails on its first generated case on a developer laptop, on main as well as with the test-depth change, with `Selected repository: default branch failed` (`DefaultUnknown`); the cause, likely something in the machine's own Git setup that the law does not pin, was not found.
proof: On a worktree at 4120e0500 (main, no change), `vitest run next/packages/libfabrika/src/node/repositories/RepositoriesGit.test.ts -t "L1: every prefix" --maxWorkers=1` with Node 26.13.0 printed `Property failed after 1 tests`, `{ seed: 119120, path: "0:1:1:1", endOnFailure: true }`, `Counterexample: ["sha256","trunk-a",[0]]`, `Caused by: RepositoriesError: Selected repository: default branch failed.` The same failure, same counterexample, came twice on the test-depth branch. The same file's two L2 laws also time out on that laptop at main (`Test timed out in 144000ms`), since their limit allows 10 ms per Git command.
cost: A person cannot run the repository laws on their own machine and trust a red result, so a real break in RepositoriesGit can hide behind this one until CI runs it.
